public_rationale: Reuters reported on March 26, 2026 that OpenAI's US advertising pilot exceeded $100 million in annualized revenue within six weeks [e1]. Dividing that reference amount by 12 gives about $8.3 million per month, an equivalent revenue pace rather than measured monthly receipts [e1]. Digiday's January 21 report attributed a 2026 advertising revenue ambition of 'low billions' to the Financial Times [e3]. These figures support the comparison of the pilot's reported scale with the larger annual ambition, without establishing a full-year shortfall [e1, e3]. The pilot began February 9 for US adults on Free and Go plans [e4]. The 'fewer than 20%' figure described daily ad exposure within the US pilot, rather than participation across all ChatGPT users [e1].
limitations: The evidence does not disclose completed-month receipts, the annualization method or an exact revenue ceiling [e1, e2].
The milestone was exceeded within six weeks; 'two months' is only a rough description of the pilot period [e1, e4].
The annual ambition is available through secondary attribution, and these reports do not establish the eventual 2026 result [e1, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's ad trial produced only about $8.3 million a month, well short of hoped-for 'low billions' in 2026.

statement.excerpt: Meanwhile, OpenAI’s attempts to bring advertising to its users have been a little embarrassing, with a two-month-long trial involving “less than 20%” of ChatGPT users resulting in “$100 million in annualized revenue,” better known as about $8.3 million in a month
statement.document_title: The Subprime AI Crisis Is Here

our_interpretation: Because the sentence explicitly starts from annualized revenue, read $8.3 million as its monthly run-rate equivalent, not verified receipts for a completed month.
Assess the reported pilot scale and its arithmetic comparison with the reported annual target. Do not interpret this as an established failure to meet the 2026 target.
Treat two months as a rough description of the February–March pilot. The exact reported milestone was reached within six weeks.
Use February–March 2026 as the observation period described by the sentence. The January announcement of the annual target is contextual evidence.
Use estimate for the press-reported financial figure; the separate company disclosure is corroborating context.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous reporting places the pilot near a $100 million annualized revenue scale, equivalent to approximately $8.3 million per month, and reports an annual 2026 advertising ambition in the low billions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable reporting establishes a materially different pilot run rate or shows that the alleged annual target was misreported. Actual monthly receipts cannot be inferred solely from an annualized figure.

evidence.locator: Headline; supporting details in opening paragraph
evidence.explanation: Reuters reports the milestone from an OpenAI spokesperson. Dividing the quoted $100 million reference amount by 12 gives approximately $8.3 million per month; the report says the milestone was exceeded, not that this was an exact revenue ceiling.
The company corroborates the annualized milestone and shorter duration. Its company-reported basis is distinguished from the contract's press-reported estimate.
This corroborates the existence of the reported 2026 ambition. It concerns a full-year target rather than the pilot's annualized run rate; the FT original could not be read.

evidence.locator: Original announcement under 'Originally published on February 9, 2026'
evidence.explanation: The launch date shows that the pilot had run for less than two full months by publication. The announcement limits the original test to US adults on Free and Go tiers.
